methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 5 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Airship Industries is a seed-stage company in the Drones & Autonomous sector. The relevant comparable universe consists of 7 private companies operating in this space, including Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air. No public market comparables exist in this narrow segment, limiting traditional public market benchmarking.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this valuation. Although 5 same-sector peers were identified, none satisfied the filtering criteria of matching stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier simultaneously. Applying a broad all-sector median would introduce excessive noise and misrepresent Airship's specific market position. With zero same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting the three-datapoint minimum threshold, traditional comparable company analysis cannot be reliably executed.

This analysis cannot support a triangulated valuation range without additional quantitative inputs on the comparable set's relevant multiples, revenue, or funding rounds. Key uncertainties include the lack of granular financial or funding data on identified peers, absence of public market anchors, and the seed stage's inherent information asymmetry. Any valuation determination would require either: expansion of the dataset to capture peer-level metrics (revenue multiples, post-money valuations from recent rounds), primary market intelligence on recent seed funding in this subsector, or application of alternative methods such as discounted cash flow analysis if forward-looking financials are available.
